signals.country: UK — effect across all 17 footprint countries
signals.signal: The UK Competition and Markets Authority FORMALLY LAUNCHED its Phase 1 merger investigation into The Brink's Company / NCR Atleos Corporation on 26/08/2026 and published a commencement notice the same day, setting a statutory Phase 1 decision deadline of 22/10/2026. This is a hard change from the 15/07/2026 position, when the case sat only at the pre-Phase-1 invitation-to-comment stage (comments closed 04/06/2026) with no statutory deadline and the widely-quoted '14 Aug 2026' date was press speculation the regulator never confirmed. The CMA will decide both whether the deal even falls within the UK merger regime and whether it substantially lessens competition; the page notes the deadline can be extended in limited circumstances. Brink's is global; NCR Atleos is global.
signals.source_name: UK Competition and Markets Authority — The Brink's Company / NCR Atleos Corporation merger inquiry case page
signals.implies: This is the single biggest structural question hanging over Printec's business, because NCR Atleos is Printec's key ATM hardware and software partner and Brink's is simultaneously a direct competitor to Printec in Greece, Romania, Czechia and Cyprus. If the deal completes, Printec's supplier becomes a subsidiary of a firm that bids against Printec for ATM managed services in four of its markets. Printec should use the 22/10/2026 CMA milestone as the trigger date for a formal channel-continuity conversation with NCR Atleos — written assurances on distributor terms, x-core multivendor software roadmap and spare-parts supply — and should have a contingency multivendor position ready before the decision lands.
signals.likelihood: Very likely to reach a Phase 1 decision by 22/10/2026; a Phase 2 reference or remedies would push the close beyond Q1 2027
signals.followup: Re-check the CMA case page on/after 22/10/2026 for the Phase 1 decision, any undertakings-in-lieu offer, or a Phase 2 reference; also watch for an EU or national merger filing, which is still not visible anywhere in the public record.

signals.signal: On the Q2 2026 earnings call (results released 05/08/2026), CEO Mark Eubanks disclosed a NEW win: 'In the AMS business, we were recently awarded a full ATM outsourcing agreement for a network consortium of banks in Europe that will come online over the second half of the year.' AMS = ATM Managed Services, i.e. the bank hands its entire ATM estate — hardware, software, cash replenishment, monitoring, first- and second-line maintenance — to Brink's on a per-transaction or per-ATM fee. Neither the country, the consortium members nor the estate size were disclosed. Eubanks framed it as part of a European structural shift: 'In Europe, we've certainly seen more activities by financial institutions to either outsource networks... There's also been banks taking another route building out their cooperatives or consortiums.' Brink's cited its existing outsourcing of BPCE in France (over 10,000 locations) as the template. Brink's is a global player.
signals.source_name: Brink's (BCO) Q2 2026 earnings call transcript, The Motley Fool
signals.implies: An ATM consortium is the model that most directly removes Printec's addressable market: when several banks pool their ATM estates into one shared network and outsource it whole, individual banks stop buying NCR ATMs, x-core multivendor software, telemetry and field services separately — one contract replaces five. Printec cannot yet name the country, but it should treat every footprint market where interbank ATM pooling is under discussion — Greece above all, where a common-name shared ATM network has been under examination since the DIAS free-withdrawal change — as at risk, and get in front of it by pitching x-core plus OptiCash plus managed services AS the consortium's technology layer rather than waiting to lose the whole estate to a Brink's end-to-end bid.
signals.likelihood: Certain to go live in H2 2026; likelihood a footprint country is next is moderate given Europe is already Brink's most-outsourced region
signals.followup: Identify the consortium — watch Brink's Q3 2026 call (due ~early November 2026) and European bank press for a named ATM-pooling joint venture; separately test each footprint market's banking association for live ATM-pooling discussions before a tender exists.

signals.country: Europe segment (includes Greece, Romania, Czechia, Cyprus)
signals.signal: Brink's Q2 2026 investor slides (results 05/08/2026) show Europe delivered the group's strongest EBITDA growth — up 19% year-on-year, 15% in constant currency — with segment margin expanding to 18.7% from 16.6%. The slides attribute this to Europe carrying a 46% AMS/DRS revenue mix, the HIGHEST of any Brink's region, explicitly credited to 'strong ATM outsourcing trends and consortium banking models that are more prevalent in European markets'. Europe's ORGANIC revenue growth was only 2%, the same as North America and Latin America, so the margin gain is a mix shift out of low-margin cash-in-transit into high-margin ATM managed services, not volume. Group AMS/DRS grew 14% organically — a 14th consecutive quarter of mid-teens-or-better growth — and Brink's targets AMS/DRS at 30-32% of total revenue in 2026, guiding mid-to-high-teens AMS/DRS organic growth for the full year. Group Q2 revenue was USD 1.39bn, up 7%, with record Q2 margins of 18.5%.
signals.source_name: Brink's Q2 2026 investor slides, reported by Investing.com; corroborated by TipRanks on the 05/08/2026 press release
signals.implies: This is the number Printec should put in front of its bank customers: Brink's makes far more margin managing a bank's ATMs than moving its cash, so every CIT relationship Brink's already holds in Greece, Romania, Czechia and Cyprus is an active upsell funnel into full ATM outsourcing — and Brink's has an explicit corporate target to grow that mix. Printec's defensive move is to reach the same accounts first with the components of the outsourcing bundle it already owns (x-core multivendor software, ATM telemetry and monitoring, APTRA OptiCash cash optimisation, field services), positioning a co-sourced model where the bank keeps the estate and Printec runs the technology, rather than conceding the whole stack.
signals.likelihood: High — the mix shift is a stated corporate strategy, not a one-off
signals.followup: Pull the actual Q2 2026 8-K exhibit 99.1 segment table from SEC EDGAR for the Europe revenue line in USD (the press release itself would not load this run); re-check the Q3 slides for whether the Europe AMS/DRS mix moves past 46%.

signals.signal: On the Q2 2026 call Brink's set out where the USD 6.6bn NCR Atleos acquisition stands and, notably, moved the expected close OUT to 'early in the first quarter of 2027'. Clearances obtained: US antitrust (early termination of the HSR waiting period), plus Brazil, India, Turkey and Colombia; foreign-direct-investment clearances in France, Germany, Spain, Italy and the United Kingdom; and money-transmitter licensing in more than 80% of the necessary jurisdictions. Both shareholder votes passed on 30/06/2026. NOTE THE DISTINCTION — the UK item management referenced is an FDI clearance, NOT a merger-control clearance; the UK CMA's competition review only formally began on 26/08/2026, three weeks after the call, and runs to 22/10/2026. No EU or other national merger filing is visible in the public record.
signals.source_name: Brink's (BCO) Q2 2026 earnings call transcript, The Motley Fool
signals.implies: Printec has a concrete planning window: its NCR Atleos supply relationship is stable through at least the end of 2026, and any ownership change lands early in Q1 2027 at the earliest. That is enough runway to close 2026 NCR ATM, recycler and x-core deals on existing terms without waiting for clarity, and enough time to negotiate post-close continuity language into 2027 framework renewals with Alpha Bank, BCR, Raiffeisen Serbia, PrivatBank and the other NCR-based accounts before the counterparty's owner changes.
signals.likelihood: Close in early Q1 2027 is management's own guidance and is contingent on the CMA outcome
signals.followup: Track Brink's and NCR Atleos 8-K filings for any further shift in the close date and for the first appearance of an EU merger filing; ask NCR Atleos directly for written distributor-continuity terms ahead of the CMA decision.

signals.entity: Brink's x KAL ATM Software (global vendor + specialist software house)
signals.signal: [STANDING — dated 2025] Re-verified this run: the Brink's–KAL ATM-as-a-Service programme, built on Brink's minority investment in KAL announced 12/06/2025, is STILL described by both parties as validated only through deployments in Asia, the United Kingdom and the Middle East. No deployment, pilot or named customer in any of Printec's 17 footprint countries could be found on KAL's or Brink's newsrooms, in the Q2 2026 results materials, or in local-language press. ATMaaS means the bank pays a per-ATM or per-transaction fee and the provider owns hardware, software and operations end to end; KAL's Kalignite is hardware-independent multivendor ATM software, the direct functional rival to Printec's x-core. Brink's brinks-ams.com newsroom carries no dated 2026 item at all.
signals.source_name: KAL ATM Software / Brink's joint announcement page (Brink's investor newsroom)
signals.implies: The good news for Printec is that the combined Brink's+KAL end-to-end ATMaaS proposition has still not been commercially proven in any Printec market, so x-core is not yet facing it head-on in a live footprint bid. The urgency is that Mellon has already brought the two parties into the region — it hosted KAL and Brink's at its ATM Innovation & Strategy Forum in Athens on 01/04/2026 on the themes of ATM modernisation and pooling. Printec should assume the first footprint ATMaaS bid arrives through that Mellon-Athens channel and should pre-position x-core plus its own managed-services wrap at Greek and Romanian banks now, while the rival stack is still unreferenced locally.
signals.likelihood: Moderate that a first footprint ATMaaS reference appears within 12 months, most likely Greece via Mellon
signals.followup: Monitor kal.com newsroom (note: kal.com returned an SSL certificate-verification failure to the fetch tool this run and needs a browser retry) and brinks-ams.com for the first named CEE/SEE ATMaaS customer.

signals.entity: Loomis AB (global/regional; Loomis Österreich GmbH and Loomis Slovakia s.r.o. are in footprint)
signals.signal: Loomis published its Interim Report January–June 2026 on 24/07/2026. Q2 2026 revenue was SEK 7,891m with currency-adjusted growth of 9.1%; operating income (EBITA) exceeded SEK 1,000m and the EBITA margin rose more than one percentage point year-on-year to 14.0%. CEO Aritz Larrea attributed the performance to both Segment USA and Segment Europe and Latin America, driven by the 'International and Automated Solutions' business lines — Automated Solutions being Loomis's cash-recycling and smart-safe hardware-and-service line, the direct analogue of Brink's DRS and a functional rival to Printec's Glory/Sesami TCR and NCR recycler business. The only acquisitions announced in the period were Transportadora del Interior (Argentina) and Hermes Transportes Blindados (Peru) — no European M&A and no Austrian or Slovak country commentary. Currency is Swedish krona.
signals.source_name: Loomis AB Interim Report January–June 2026 (company release distributed via PR Newswire)
signals.implies: Loomis is growing its Automated Solutions line — recyclers and smart safes sold as a managed service — faster than its CIT base, which puts it in direct competition with Printec's Glory and Sesami teller-cash-recycler and NCR recycler proposition in Austria and Slovakia. It is also the most plausible non-Brink's bidder for the still-unawarded Geldservice Austria EUR 9.1m recycler framework (TED 305531-2026, contract start 02/11/2026). Printec should treat that framework as a two-horse race against Loomis and Diebold Nixdorf and price the service wrap, not just the hardware.
signals.likelihood: High that Loomis bids Austrian cash-automation work; the GSA framework award is due before 02/11/2026
signals.followup: Open the full Loomis H1 2026 PDF for the Segment Europe and Latin America revenue and EBITA lines and any Austria/Slovakia commentary — loomis.com/en/investors/financial-reports returned HTTP 404 this run and the report URL needs to be relocated.
